styleWhy: A zipper is a small machine you understand by taking it apart, so line drawings that cut it open and label each part show the mechanism clearly.

copy.idea: A zipper is two rows of identical teeth and one slider. Each tooth has a recess on one side and a projection on the other, so the teeth of one row nest into the teeth of the other. The slider is a sliding cam: moved one way it meshes the teeth, moved the other way it separates them.
copy.hook: Tiny teeth, no glue: so how does a zipper hold?
copy.body:
Every tooth has the same shape: a bump on top and a hollow underneath.

The teeth on one side alternate with the teeth on the other, offset by half a tooth, so each tooth lines up with a gap opposite.

The slider is a Y-shaped channel. As you pull it up, it brings the two rows together and nests each tooth's bump in the hollow of the tooth beside it.

Once the teeth are locked, each one sits nested in the next, and the row stays shut.

To open it, slide it back: the same channel separates the teeth, one at a time.

The design was patented in 1917 as a 'separable fastener'.

facts.text: Each tooth has a hollow on one side and a bump on the other. Quoted: "a rounded recess on one side and a corresponding projection on the opposite side"
facts.source: Gideon Sundback, US Patent 1,219,881 "Separable fastener", granted 20 March 1917, https://patents.google.com/patent/US1219881

facts.text: Locked teeth nest inside each other. Quoted: "the outside of one member nests within the recess of an adjoining member when in locked relation"
facts.source: Gideon Sundback, US Patent 1,219,881 "Separable fastener", granted 20 March 1917, https://patents.google.com/patent/US1219881

facts.text: The two rows alternate. Quoted: "The members on one stringer alternate with those on the other". Shown as an offset of half a tooth: with evenly spaced teeth, alternating means each tooth faces the gap opposite, half a pitch along; that is our reading, not a quote.
facts.source: Gideon Sundback, US Patent 1,219,881 "Separable fastener", granted 20 March 1917, https://patents.google.com/patent/US1219881

facts.text: The slider locks or unlocks depending on which way it moves. Quoted: "a sliding cam operating device" that locks and unlocks "according to its direction of movement"
facts.source: Gideon Sundback, US Patent 1,219,881 "Separable fastener", granted 20 March 1917, https://patents.google.com/patent/US1219881

facts.text: The slider's channel is Y-shaped. Quoted: "The slider, usually operated by hand, contains a Y-shaped channel that, by moving along the rows of teeth, meshes or separates them, depending on the direction of the slider's movement." Read from the search snippet; the page itself could not be loaded.
Patented in 1917 as a 'separable fastener'. Title on the patent: "Separable fastener", granted 20 March 1917.

shots.title: Hook: the zipper
shots.show: A tall vertical zipper fills the frame on the blueprint grid: the two fabric tapes and two rows of teeth (left row blue, right row amber) draw on stroke by stroke from top to bottom, open in a V. The slider draws on at the bottom and rides up, closing the teeth behind it into one interlocked column. A callout line snaps out to the slider: 'slider'; another to the teeth: 'teeth'.
shots.text: Tiny teeth, no glue: how does it hold?
shots.motion: Line art traces on; slider travels up with an ease, teeth clicking shut in sequence behind it; the camera eases in slightly.

shots.title: One tooth, exploded
shots.show: Close-up of the zipper column; one blue tooth lifts out and slides into an exploded view at full size in the centre, rotating to a 3/4 section view and cut open. Callouts draw on: 'bump' pointing to the raised top, 'hollow' to the pocket underneath, with a dimension line across its width. A ghost of the next tooth slides under it to show the bump will sit in that hollow.
shots.text: Every tooth: bump above, hollow below
shots.motion: Tooth lifts and slides apart from the row, section hatching fills in, callout lines extend and labels type on, the ghost tooth glides into place.

shots.title: Two rows, offset
shots.show: Top view of the two rows of teeth on their tapes, left row blue, right row amber, facing each other across a gap. A dimension marker measures one tooth pitch, then a half-pitch marker shows the right row shifted down by half a tooth. Dashed guide lines from each blue tooth point into a gap on the amber side; the rows slide together and alternate, tooth by tooth.
shots.text: Two rows, offset by half a tooth
shots.motion: Dimension lines draw on, the amber row shifts half a pitch, dashed guides flash, then both rows slide inward and interleave.

shots.title: Inside the slider
shots.show: The slider is cut open into a Y-shaped channel, drawn large and centred: two upper arms, one lower throat, labelled 'Y-channel' and 'divider'. Blue teeth stream in through the left arm, amber through the right; as the arms bring them together in the throat each tooth turns flat (an arc marks the turn), its bump nests in the next tooth's hollow, and the meshed column exits at the bottom. Each tooth pulses teal as it locks.
shots.text: The slider nests tooth into tooth
shots.motion: Teeth flow continuously through the channel, angle arcs open and close at the meeting point, teal lock pulses run down the exiting column.
shots.source: Gideon Sundback, US Patent 1,219,881 "Separable fastener", 1917; Encyclopaedia Britannica, "zipper"

shots.title: Why it holds
shots.show: The closed zipper column, side by side with a cross-section strip of locked teeth, each bump nested in the next tooth's hollow. Red force arrows pull the left and right tapes outward and run along the row while each bump-in-hollow lock glows teal and does not move. A 'pull' label with growing arrow lengths shows the force rising; the column stays shut.
shots.text: Locked, each tooth sits nested in the next
shots.motion: Red arrows grow outward and tremble, the force fans out tooth by tooth down the column, teal locks pulse steadily, the teeth stay put.

shots.title: Slide it back to open
shots.show: The same cut-open slider Y-channel as shot 4, now moving down the closed column: the same slider, moving the other way. The divider between the arms (outlined amber-white) parts the meshed teeth; each tooth turns along the same arc and unnests, blue going out the left arm, amber the right. A counter-arrow and a callout read 'one tooth at a time'.
shots.text: Slide it back: it separates them
shots.motion: Slider glides down, teeth unhook in sequence with a small tilt and spring apart into the arms, teal lock glows switching off as each tooth leaves.
shots.source: Gideon Sundback, US Patent 1,219,881 "Separable fastener", 1917; Encyclopaedia Britannica, "zipper"

shots.title: End card
shots.show: The full zipper from shot 1 zips shut one last time, its slider reaching the top. Beside it a patent-style title block draws on, like a drawing's corner stamp: 'SEPARABLE FASTENER', with the year rolling up to 1917.
shots.motion: Slider races up, title-block border traces on, year counter rolls and lands with a bounce.

recurring.name: Zipper column
recurring.design: Vertical zipper centred in the frame: two fabric tapes drawn as hatched strips, left row of teeth blue, right row amber, slider at the bottom when open or top when closed, pull tab hanging down. Line art in the look's white ink on the grid; teal glow means a tooth is locked, red means force.

recurring.name: Tooth shape
recurring.design: Each tooth drawn the same: a rounded rectangular head with a raised bump on top and a hollow pocket underneath, labelled 'bump' and 'hollow'; blue on the left row, amber on the right.

recurring.design: Large cut-open slider centred: Y-shaped channel with two arms at the top (left arm takes blue teeth, right arm amber) and the throat at the bottom, a divider between the arms, labels 'Y-channel' and 'divider', and an angle arc at the meeting point.
